public_source.verification_note: Task ids are selected from terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 registry task_id_subset; no local invented tasks are allowed.

benefit_gate.claimed_engineering_benefit: R4 final acceptance stresses real public tool-use tasks and reports per-sample standard vs TaskSpace correctness, latency, token, cache, projection, and tool-feedback behavior.
benefit_gate.baseline: R4 known-bad samples alone cannot prove broad tool-chain quality; public-sample selection and report fields were previously Markdown-only.
benefit_gate.pass_threshold: exactly 10 public samples; every sample has source metadata and tool-stress rationale; final report has one row per sample with all required tool/cost/performance fields.

samples.tool_stress_focus: script creation, text processing, command output validation
samples.why_selected: Exercises file creation, command execution, stdout comparison, and validator feedback without heavyweight toolchain, locked permission fixtures, or unpinned remote runtime assets.
Exercises multi-step shell feedback and environment state judgment.
Exercises repeated command feedback and recovery behavior.

samples.tool_stress_focus: git state inspection, branch and file operations
samples.why_selected: Exercises state semantics and path attribution in tool results.
Exercises stdout/stderr influence on later decisions.
Exercises tool output, permissions, and safety-semantics fidelity.

samples.tool_stress_focus: database commands, compile and coverage output
samples.why_selected: Exercises structured failure parsing and validator feedback.
Exercises intermediate artifacts, changed paths, and test feedback.
Exercises file checks, command output, and artifact validation.
Exercises non-trivial terminal interaction and tool-call ordering.

tool_analysis_questions: Was the tool-call intent executed or rejected correctly?
Did the tool result enter the next provider payload with standard-equivalent semantics?
Were stderr, stdout, path, and exit code retained, summarized, ref-backed, or lost?
Did the TaskSpace map record the same semantics and attribution?
Did repeated failures produce semantic progress or a loop?
What were TaskSpace wall, token, and tool-call multipliers versus standard?
